title: Refactor Terraform networking templates into reusable modules and upgrade cloud providers
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Over the last three years we accumulated multiple environment-specific Terraform network templates (staging, prod, dedicated, private) with duplicated CIDR/route/security logic. This has increased drift, made cross-account upgrades brittle, and slowed onboarding for Private deployments. Goal: Consolidate networking logic into a small set of reusable Terraform modules (vpc, subnets, routing, peering/tgw, security-groups), upgrade AWS and GCP providers to the latest supported major versions, and update state migration templates so rolling upgrades are low-risk.

Scope:
- Create terraform/modules/{vpc,subnets,routing,security,transit} with clear inputs/outputs and consistent naming conventions.
- Replace ad-hoc env templates with thin wrappers that call modules.
- Upgrade aws provider from 3.x -> 4.x and google provider from 3.x -> 5.x (evaluate breaking changes).
- Standardize CIDR allocation logic via a shared allocator module and document VPC sizing for Dedicated/Private.
- Add automated plan validation (ci) and a drift detection job in CloudOps.

Non-goals: Full re-architecture of networking (no changes to core network topology), changing existing customer CIDRs, or changing third-party transit providers.
acceptance_criteria: All environment templates reduced to < 50 LOC wrappers that call modules
No terraform apply in staging/prod until migration path exists and one staging canary succeeds
Provider upgrades applied in a dedicated pipeline with automated plan-diff checks
Module unit examples and documentation added to the infra repo (README + usage examples)
No increased egress cost or new open security group rules introduced by refactor
tasks: Inventory existing networking TF files across infra repos
Design module interfaces (inputs/outputs) and write interface doc
Implement modules and thin wrappers for staging/prod/dedicated/private
Create migration plan for Terraform state (state mv & state import where needed)
Upgrade provider versions in a feature branch and run full plan in dry-run accounts
Add CI job: terraform fmt/validate/plan-warn and policy checks (sentinel/opa)
Run canary apply in staging account and monitor network tests
Schedule prod rollout with maintenance window and rollback plan
notes:
Key risk: provider major upgrades include resource address/name changes (aws_lb -> aws_lb_target_group attachments) and some deprecated arguments. We will gate apply with a dry-run on a disposable account and use state backups. Tradeoff: slower rollout to avoid any IP interruptions vs faster consolidation that reduces long term drift. Chosen approach leans conservative: canary first, then batched rollout.

Rollback plan: keep previous state backup, and maintain thin wrapper templates that can revert to legacy resources if a migration fails. CI will block merges with plan diffs that remove resources without explicit approval.
